assignment.description:
📖 Assignment: Book Review of 1984 – History, Memory, and Control

Writing Assignment • Length: 3–4 pages, double spaced

📖 Lesson Access

Open the Jupyter Book lesson

🎯 Purpose

When historians write book reviews, they evaluate works of scholarship and explain their significance to the profession. In this assignment, you will practice those same skills, but with a classic work of political fiction: George Orwell’s 1984. The goal is to consider how Orwell’s story illustrates the dangers of manipulated history and the loss of historical memory.

As you read, reflect on the guiding question:

What happens to a society when it no longer has a reliable historical memory?

🧩 Format of Your Review

Your review should follow a structured format and maintain a clear, scholarly tone. Avoid personal opinion or casual commentary—support your ideas with examples from the novel.

  1. Title
    Create a short, focused title for your review that highlights both the book and the theme.
    Example: “Who Controls the Past: Historical Memory in Orwell’s 1984.”
  2. Introduction
    Begin with the title and author of the novel.
    Briefly explain why 1984 matters for students of history and society.
    State the central question of your review: how Orwell warns about the consequences of erasing or rewriting history.
  3. Summary of the Novel
    Provide a concise summary of the main plot points.
    Highlight key features related to historical memory:
    • Winston’s work at the Ministry of Truth
    • The slogan “Who controls the past controls the future.”
    • The Party’s systematic rewriting of the record
  4. Author’s Thesis and Message
    Since Orwell is not a historian, identify his message instead of a formal thesis.
    Explain how the novel shows the relationship between memory, truth, and power.
    Discuss how the Party’s manipulation of history serves as a tool of control.
  5. Structure and Organization
    Comment on the way Orwell builds the narrative (Winston’s perspective, the gradual destruction of resistance).
    Reflect on how this structure reinforces the theme of memory and forgetting.
  6. Historical Context and Connections
    Connect the novel’s themes to real historical examples: propaganda, censorship, erasure of records, or rewriting history.
    Draw parallels to present-day concerns: misinformation, media manipulation, or the fragility of historical truth in a digital age.
    Answer: What lessons can historians and citizens learn from 1984 about preserving memory?
  7. Strengths and Weaknesses
    Identify strengths: Orwell’s prescience, his insight into propaganda and control.
    Identify weaknesses: the limits of fiction as historical evidence.
    Reflect on what fiction can accomplish that historical monographs cannot.
  8. Conclusion
    Summarize your overall assessment of the novel’s warning.
    Conclude with your reflection on the guiding question:
    What safeguards does a society need to protect historical memory and prevent the manipulation of truth?

📝 Reminders

  • Use a clear, academic tone.
  • Support your points with examples from the novel.
  • Do not substitute internet summaries for your own careful reading.
  • Length: 3–4 pages, double spaced.

Academic Integrity Reminder: There is no need to use AI tools to complete this assignment. You may use AI to help you format or polish your writing, but your ideas, analysis, and examples must be entirely your own. Submitting AI-generated work as your own is considered academic dishonesty.
